'Blade of Demon Destruction') is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotouge. It was serialized in Shueisha's shōnen manga magazine Weekly Shōnen Jump from February 2016 to May 2020, with its chapters collected in 23 tankōbon volumes.

Meaning is not found in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — it is manufactured for it. It has been published in English by Viz Media and simultaneously on the Manga Plus platform by Shueisha. It follows teenage Tanjiro Kamado, who joins the Demon Slayer Corps after his family is slaughtered and the sole survivor, his younger sister Nezuko, is turned into a demon, in the hopes of turning her human again.

The cold light on Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. An 18-episode second season of the anime series aired from October 2021 to February 2022 while a feature-length compilation, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – To the Swordsmith Village, was released in theaters in February 2023. An 11-episode third season aired from April to June 2023 while another compilation, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – To the Hashira Training, was released in theaters in February 2024.

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. A film trilogy sequel adapting the "Infinity Castle" story arc premiered in theaters in July 2025. By July 2025, the manga had over 220 million copies in circulation, including digital versions, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time; it was the best-selling manga of 2019 and 2020.

The honest version of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba starts by giving up the comforting part. The Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba franchise is one of the highest-grossing media franchises of all time. In Taishō era Japan, a secret organization known as the "Demon Slayer Corps" has waged a war against demons for centuries.

Strip Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Demons are former humans who possess supernatural abilities such as enhanced strength, rapid regeneration, and unique powers referred to as "Blood Demon Arts". Demons can only be killed if they are exposed to direct sunlight, decapitated with weapons crafted from an alloy called Nichirin, or injected with a poison extracted from wisteria flowers.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba shows exactly where that breaks. In contrast, the Demon Slayers are entirely human but employ specialized elemental breathing techniques known as "Breathing Styles". These techniques grant them superhuman strength, heightened abilities, and increased resilience that enable them to fight demons effectively.

What looks like free choice in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is older than choice itself. The most formidable Demon Slayers are known as the "Hashira" and gain this title through multiple advancements in the Corps' ranks, culminating in killing fifty demons at the highest level or a member of the Twelve Kizuki. Tanjiro Kamado is a kind-hearted and diligent boy who lives with his family in the mountains.

Nobody designed the part of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba you experience — it was inherited. After the death of his father, he becomes the sole provider for his household, selling charcoal in nearby villages. His younger sister, Nezuko, is the only survivor, though she has been transformed into a demon herself.

Every serious account of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. The pair are discovered by Giyu Tomioka, the Water Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps, who sends Tanjiro to be trained by his own former mentor, Sakonji Urokodaki. Tanjiro vows to become a Demon Slayer to avenge his family and find a way to return Nezuko to humanity.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. After mastering the "Water Breathing" swordsmanship style, Tanjiro passes the Corps' final selection. Nezuko, who has been placed under a hypnotic suggestion by Urokodaki to suppress her demonic urges, accompanies him.

The selfish-gene reading of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba makes it less romantic and far more precise. During a mission in Asakusa, they encounter Muzan Kibutsuji, the progenitor of all demons and the one responsible for the murder of their family. They also befriend Tamayo and her assistant Yushiro, two demons who have freed themselves from Muzan's control.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. Tamayo agrees to develop a cure for Nezuko, a process that requires blood from the powerful Twelve Kizuki, Muzan's most elite subordinates. Tanjiro and Nezuko are joined in their mission by fellow Demon Slayers Zenitsu Agatsuma and Inosuke Hashibira.

The feeling that Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. During a fierce battle, Tanjiro awakens a mysterious and powerful swordsmanship technique known as "Hinokami Kagura". Their actions draw the attention of the Hashira, the Corps' highest-ranking swordsmen, and they are brought before the organization's leader, Kagaya Ubuyashiki.

Nothing in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Muzan, enraged by the failures of his remaining Lower Ranks, executes all of them except for Lower One, who he sends to kill Tanjiro. After a battle aboard a moving train, Tanjiro prevails with the aid of the Flame Hashira, Kyojuro Rengoku, who is subsequently killed by the Upper Three demon, Akaza.

The psychology underneath Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is simpler and older than the story on top. The group continues their campaign, assisting the Sound Hashira in defeating the Upper Six siblings and later helping the Mist and Love Hashira eliminate Upper Five and Upper Four at the Swordsmith Village. During these events, Nezuko develops an immunity to sunlight, making her the key to Muzan's goal of overcoming his own fatal weakness.

Behind Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. Tanjiro also learns that his Hinokami Kagura is derived from "Sun Breathing", the original swordsmanship style created by Breathing progenitor Yoriichi Tsugikuni. The Demon Slayer Corps prepares for a final confrontation as Tamayo works on a serum.

The nihilist does not deny Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — he only refuses to flatter it. Muzan launches a preemptive assault, prompting Kagaya to sacrifice himself in a suicide attack. The Hashira engage Muzan, but he traps them within the Infinity Castle, where they must battle the remaining Upper Ranks.

What culture calls destiny in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. Muzan kills Tamayo but is severely weakened by the poison she implanted in him. Forced above ground, a desperate battle ensues as the remaining Demon Slayers fight to hold him until sunrise.

The genes do not care about Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba; they care about copies. With his last breath, Muzan transforms Tanjiro into a demon, but Nezuko, now fully human, helps reverse the transformation. In the aftermath of Muzan's defeat, all demons under his control perish.

Take away the meaning and Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba still functions — that is the disturbing part. The Demon Slayer Corps is disbanded, with only two of the active Hashira surviving. Tanjiro and Nezuko return to their mountain home, their journey finally complete.

The unconscious does not argue with Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba; it simply acts first. In the ensuing years, Tanjiro marries Kanao Tsuyuri, Inosuke weds Aoi Kanzaki, and Zenitsu marries Nezuko. In a modern-day epilogue, their descendants and reincarnations live in a world free from demons.

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. After Gotouge's previous manga, Haeniwa no Zigzag, published in Weekly Shōnen Jump in 2015, failed to become a serialized work, Tatsuhiko Katayama, Gotouge's first editor, suggested Gotouge to start a series with an "easy-to-understand theme". Gotouge's debut work Kagarigari would become the basis for an initial draft, titled Kisatsu no Nagare (鬼殺の流れ) since it had concepts like swords and demons, which would be familiar to the Japanese audience.

The bleak reading of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is also the most testable one. However, due to its serious tone, lack of comic relief, and dark story, this draft was not accepted for serialization, so Katayama asked Gotouge to try writing a brighter, more average character in the same setting. The original title was Kisatsu no Yaiba (鬼殺の刃), but they felt the character satsu (殺; lit. 'kill') in the title was too overt.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba. Although it is a made-up word, "kimetsu" (鬼滅) seemed easy to understand, so Gotouge thought it would be interesting to abbreviate the series' title that way; the word yaiba (刃; lit. 'blade') implies a Japanese sword. According to Gotouge, the series' three biggest influences are JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Naruto, and Bleach.

The self that experiences Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is a committee, not a king. The series' first editor, Tatsuhiko Katayama, stated that Tanjiro was partially influenced by Himura Kenshin, the protagonist of Rurouni Kenshin. Written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotouge, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba was serialized in Shueisha's shōnen manga magazine Weekly Shōnen Jump from February 15, 2016, to May 18, 2020.
